The Nigerian champions confirmed their position in a statement on Thursday after CAF’s Appeal Board upheld an earlier decision to cancel their penalty-shootout win and order the final to continue from the start of extra time.
The controversy began on 5 September when Edo Queens played Ghanaian side Ampem Darkoa in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. The match was 2-2 after regulation time, but the game went straight to penalties without the required two 15-minute periods of extra time. Edo Queens won the shootout 4-1.
Ampem Darkoa, backed by the Ghana Football Association, protested, arguing that competition rules required extra time before a penalty shootout. CAF’s Organising Committee for Women’s Football later annulled the shootout result and ordered the match to resume at 2-2 from the beginning of extra time.
The Nigeria Football Federation appealed on Edo Queens’ behalf, arguing that the Nigerian club should not be punished for an error by match officials. However, CAF’s Appeal Board ruled on 16 October that the shootout victory had no sporting effect and that the final must continue from extra time.
The resumption will consist of two 15-minute periods. If the teams remain level, a new penalty shootout will decide the winner. CAF also directed that different match officials be appointed for the continuation.
Edo Queens said they decided to accept the ruling after consultations with their board, the Edo State Government and the NFF. The club admitted the outcome was not what they had hoped for but said proceeding with the match would allow both teams to settle the contest on the pitch.
The club thanked the Edo State Government and the NFF for their support during the appeal, as well as their fans and the media for standing by the team. Edo Queens said their focus had now shifted to the decisive encounter in Cairo.
The club said its mission remained to fight, win and secure a place in the CAF Women’s Champions League. It urged supporters to keep backing the team and promised that the players and technical crew would give their all against Ampem Darkoa.
The winner of the resumed final will represent WAFU-B at the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League, scheduled to be held in Egypt from 1 to 5 November.
